```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = "..")
```

```{r packages}
source("scripts/setup.R")
source("analysis/dgp-helpers.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyfun)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
})
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
cells <- design_table()
N_SHOW <- 25 # curves shown per spaghetti plot

# One cell of the design, found by its factors.
get_cell <- function(...) {
  keys <- list(...)
  hit <- Reduce(`&`, Map(\(k, v) cells[[k]] == v, names(keys), keys))
  as.list(cells[which(hit)[1], ])
}

# A matrix (rows = curves) on grid `arg` as a data frame with one tf column.
curves <- function(mat, arg, ...) {
  d <- data.frame(id = seq_len(nrow(mat)), ...)
  d$f <- tfd(mat, arg = arg)
  d
}

spaghetti <- function(d, colour = NULL, title = NULL, ylab = NULL) {
  aes_col <- if (is.null(colour)) aes(y = f) else aes(y = f, colour = .data[[colour]])
  p <- ggplot(d, aes_col) +
    geom_spaghetti(linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.8) +
    labs(title = title, x = "t", y = ylab)
  if (is.null(colour)) p + aes(group = id) else p
}

# Diverging fill with a neutral midpoint for signed surfaces and correlations.
diverging <- function(name, limits = NULL) {
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    name = name, low = "#2166ac", mid = "grey96", high = "#b2182b",
    midpoint = 0, limits = limits
  )
}

surface_plot <- function(z, x, y, xlab, ylab, title, name = "value", limits = NULL) {
  d <- expand.grid(x = x, y = y)
  d$z <- as.vector(z)
  ggplot(d, aes(x, y, fill = z)) +
    geom_raster() +
    diverging(name, limits) +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = title)
}
```

This document shows what the study simulates. Everything is computed from the study code
(`R/`), with the same functions and constants as the production runs; the replicate shown is
replicate 1 unless noted.

## Covariates

```{r covariates}
#| fig-height: 3.5
draws <- draw_replicate(1)
cov <- make_covariates(draws$xi, draws$z, draws$x)
eig <- svd(scale(cov$X, scale = FALSE), nu = 0, nv = 0)$d^2
share <- eig / sum(eig)
p_x <- spaghetti(
  curves(cov$X[1:N_SHOW, ], S_GRID, level = cov$X[1:N_SHOW, 1]),
  title = "Functional covariate X_i(s), 25 of 100 curves", ylab = "X(s)"
) + labs(x = "s")
p_eig <- ggplot(data.frame(k = 1:15, share = share[1:15]), aes(k, share)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, fill = "#2166ac") +
  labs(title = "Eigenvalue shares", x = "component", y = "share")
p_x + p_eig + plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1))
```

The first component explains `r round(100 * share[1])`% of the centred variance, the first
four `r round(100 * sum(share[1:4]))`%; the 99.5% effective rank of this sample is
`r centred_rank(cov$X)` (the fitted ff basis has 8 functions along s).

## True effects

```{r truths}
#| fig-height: 7
t <- EVAL_T
t_fine <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 101)
beta <- lapply(c(smooth = "smooth", wiggly = "wiggly"), \(r) make_truth("M1", r))
s_show <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 11)
beta_curves <- \(r) curves(beta[[r]]$beta(s_show, t_fine), t_fine, s = s_show)
p_b <- lapply(names(beta), \(r) {
  spaghetti(beta_curves(r), colour = "s",
    title = paste0("beta(s, t), ", r, ": one curve per s"), ylab = "beta") +
    scale_colour_gradient(low = "grey75", high = "#08306b")
})
lim <- max(abs(unlist(lapply(beta, \(b) b$beta(t_fine, t_fine)))))
p_s <- lapply(names(beta), \(r) {
  surface_plot(beta[[r]]$beta(t_fine, t_fine), t_fine, t_fine, "s", "t",
    paste0("beta(s, t), ", r), "beta", c(-lim, lim))
})
(p_b[[1]] + p_s[[1]]) / (p_b[[2]] + p_s[[2]])
```

```{r truths-1d}
#| fig-height: 3.5
one_d <- rbind(
  data.frame(term = "gamma(t)", truth = "smooth", t = t_fine, value = beta$smooth$gamma(t_fine)),
  data.frame(term = "gamma(t)", truth = "wiggly", t = t_fine, value = beta$wiggly$gamma(t_fine)),
  data.frame(term = "alpha(t) (bump, Gaussian)", truth = "all cells", t = t_fine,
    value = beta$smooth$bump(t_fine))
)
ggplot(one_d, aes(t, value, linetype = truth)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, colour = "#08306b") +
  facet_wrap(~term, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Varying coefficient gamma(t) and intercept alpha(t)", y = NULL)
```

```{r truth-f}
#| fig-height: 3.5
m2 <- make_truth("M2", "smooth")
x_show <- seq(0.05, 0.95, length.out = 10)
spaghetti(curves(m2$f(x_show, t_fine), t_fine, x = x_show), colour = "x",
  title = "f(x, t) of the term-type model (M2): one curve per x", ylab = "f") +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "grey75", high = "#08306b")
```

## Simulated responses

Gaussian responses at the default signal (R² = 0.5) under each error process, and the count
and binary responses of the core design (fpc errors). The same covariates and random draws
enter every panel (common random numbers).

```{r responses}
#| fig-height: 8
errors <- c("iid", "ou", "fpc", "osc", "ou0")
sim_cell <- \(cell) simulate(cell, 1)
gauss <- lapply(errors, \(e) {
  cell <- get_cell(family = "gaussian", error = e, G = 100L, signal = "mid")
  sim_cell(cell)
})
names(gauss) <- errors
warp_sim <- sim_cell(get_cell(block = "warp", family = "gaussian", G = 100L, truth = "smooth"))
panels <- c(
  lapply(errors, \(e) {
    spaghetti(curves(unclass(gauss[[e]]$data$Y)[1:N_SHOW, ], gauss[[e]]$yind),
      title = paste("Gaussian,", e), ylab = "Y")
  }),
  list(spaghetti(curves(unclass(warp_sim$data$Y)[1:N_SHOW, ], warp_sim$yind),
    title = "Gaussian, warp (high signal)", ylab = "Y"))
)
wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 2)
```

```{r responses-glm}
#| fig-height: 4.5
glm_sims <- lapply(c(poisson = "poisson", binomial = "binomial"), \(f) {
  sim_cell(get_cell(block = "core", family = f, error = "fpc", G = 100L, signal = "mid"))
})
# Responses as an image: one row per curve (40 curves), t along the x axis.
response_image <- function(sim, title, fill) {
  y <- unclass(sim$data$Y)[1:40, ]
  d <- expand.grid(curve = seq_len(nrow(y)), t = sim$yind)
  d$y <- as.vector(y)
  ggplot(d, aes(t, curve, fill = y)) +
    geom_raster() +
    fill +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = title, x = "t", y = "curve")
}
response_image(glm_sims$poisson, "Poisson counts (mean 3), fpc",
  scale_fill_gradient("count", low = "grey96", high = "#08306b", trans = "sqrt")) +
  response_image(glm_sims$binomial, "Binary (prevalence 0.2), fpc",
    scale_fill_gradient("y", low = "grey96", high = "#08306b", breaks = c(0, 1)))
```

## Residuals

Residuals Y − E(Y | X, z) for the Gaussian cells; for the warp cells E(Y | X, z) is the
observed-clock mean (the expectation over the warps).

```{r residuals}
#| fig-height: 8
resid <- c(
  lapply(setNames(errors, errors), \(e) {
    residual_curves(get_cell(family = "gaussian", error = e, G = 100L, signal = "mid"), 1)
  }),
  list(
    `warp, smooth truth` = residual_curves(
      get_cell(block = "warp", family = "gaussian", G = 100L, truth = "smooth"), 1),
    `warp, wiggly truth` = residual_curves(
      get_cell(block = "warp", family = "gaussian", G = 100L, truth = "wiggly"), 1)
  )
)
t61 <- t_grid(61)
wrap_plots(lapply(names(resid), \(n) {
  spaghetti(curves(resid[[n]][1:12, ], t61), title = n, ylab = "residual")
}), ncol = 2)
```

## Residual correlations

The correlation kernels as specified (top), and the empirical correlations of residuals pooled
over 20 replicates (2,000 curves) — including the warp cells, whose residual correlation is
not a kernel of the design but a consequence of misregistration, and the correlation of
Poisson and binary residuals (response scale) generated from the fpc latent process.

```{r kernels}
#| fig-height: 5.5
kernel_panels <- lapply(errors, \(e) {
  surface_plot(correlation_kernel(e, t61), t61, t61, "t", "t'", e, "corr", c(-1, 1))
})
wrap_plots(kernel_panels, ncol = 3, guides = "collect")
```

```{r empirical-correlations}
#| fig-height: 8
pooled_resid <- function(cell, n_rep = 20) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_rep), \(r) residual_curves(cell, r)))
}
empirical <- list(
  `fpc (Gaussian)` = get_cell(family = "gaussian", error = "fpc", G = 100L, signal = "mid"),
  `osc (Gaussian)` = get_cell(family = "gaussian", error = "osc", G = 100L, signal = "mid"),
  `warp, smooth truth` = get_cell(block = "warp", family = "gaussian", G = 100L, truth = "smooth"),
  `warp, wiggly truth` = get_cell(block = "warp", family = "gaussian", G = 100L, truth = "wiggly"),
  `fpc, Poisson` = get_cell(block = "core", family = "poisson", error = "fpc",
    G = 100L, signal = "mid"),
  `fpc, binary` = get_cell(block = "core", family = "binomial", error = "fpc",
    G = 100L, signal = "mid")
)
emp_cor <- lapply(empirical, \(cell) cor(pooled_resid(cell)))
de <- sapply(emp_cor, \(R) sum(R) / nrow(R))
wrap_plots(lapply(names(emp_cor), \(n) {
  surface_plot(emp_cor[[n]], t61, t61, "t", "t'", sprintf("%s (DE %.1f)", n, de[[n]]),
    "corr", c(-1, 1))
}), ncol = 2, guides = "collect")
```

Design effects (1ᵀR1 / tr R) of these empirical correlation matrices:
`r paste(sprintf("%s %.1f", names(de), de), collapse = "; ")`. The design effect only
measures the constant contrast; warp and osc residuals have strong sign-changing correlations
that it averages away (see the study notes on why the misregistration strength was chosen by
the true-SD/model-SE ratio instead).

## Misregistration: registered and observed-clock targets

```{r warp-targets}
#| fig-height: 3.5
quad <- warp_quadrature()
smear <- \(f) rowSums(sapply(seq_along(quad$a), \(k) quad$w[k] * f(drop(warp_times(quad$a[k], t_fine)))))
bump_reg <- beta$smooth$bump(t_fine)
bump_obs <- smear(beta$smooth$bump)
g_reg <- beta$wiggly$gamma(t_fine)
g_obs <- smear(beta$wiggly$gamma)
warp_d <- rbind(
  data.frame(term = "alpha(t)", clock = "registered", t = t_fine, value = bump_reg),
  data.frame(term = "alpha(t)", clock = "observed (smeared)", t = t_fine, value = bump_obs),
  data.frame(term = "gamma(t), wiggly", clock = "registered", t = t_fine, value = g_reg),
  data.frame(term = "gamma(t), wiggly", clock = "observed (smeared)", t = t_fine, value = g_obs)
)
ggplot(warp_d, aes(t, value, linetype = clock)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, colour = "#08306b") +
  facet_wrap(~term, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "What a common-clock fit estimates under misregistration (10% displacement)",
    y = NULL)
```

At 10% maximum displacement the smeared bump is `r round(100 * (1 - max(bump_obs) / max(bump_reg)))`%
lower than the registered one.
